transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Dr. Samuel Reed (Nimbus CISO), Jenna Ortiz (Head of Ops), Miguel Alvarez (Cloud Infra)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today. we'll run through security artifacts, incident response and then the BCDR / SLA escalation flow. priya and i will take point on the technical runbook side.
[00:12] Dr. Samuel Reed: thanks alex, we mostly want to validate the RTOs you can meet in a private deployment and how keys and logs are handled. also SOC two and the iso scope.
[00:22] Priya Malhotra: yep—quick agenda: start with compliance artifacts (SOC 2 Type II, iso 27001 scope), then auth (SSO/SCIM, RBAC), audit logs & retention, encryption/KMS options (BYOK, CMK, HSM), then IR/BCDR — RTO/RPO, on-call, runbooks, and then SLA & escalation. sound good?
[00:33] Jenna Ortiz: sounds great. we have a hard requirement for EU data residency on PHI-adjacent data.
[00:40] Miguel Alvarez: and we need customer-managed keys in eu-central if possible — we can't have Redwood hold keys for that dataset.
[00:47] Alex Chen: understood. quick note — for private deployments we support integrating with customer KMS (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys; we'll share the KMS connector spec after.
[00:56] Dr. Samuel Reed: ok, also how long do logs live? our security team wants 7 years for audit trails — is that feasible?
[01:04] Priya Malhotra: so currently our standard hosted retention is 90 days, dedicated/private we can configure longer retention and export. log archival to customer S3 in eu-central is supported — it depends on storage lifecycle and cost, but technical path exists.
[01:18] Alex Chen: we'll put that in writing. export + immutability options via object lock can be discussed.
[01:25] Speaker 1: (inaudible) um — is there an automated way to pull logs into our SIEM?
[01:30] Priya Malhotra: yes we're commonly hooking with SIEMs via streaming or via S3 export + Glue/ingestion. we also support webhook events for critical incidents.
[01:40] Dr. Samuel Reed: on auth: we use okta with SAML and SCIM provisioning for accounts. RBAC is important — least privilege. how granular is your role model?
[01:49] Priya Malhotra: we have tenant-level roles, route-level tokens, and token-scoped permissions. for private deployments we can mirror your org groups via SCIM and map to roles. there is an RBAC matrix; i'll attach that.
[02:00] Miguel Alvarez: is there auditability for role changes? we need immutable trails when someone escalates to admin.
[02:06] Priya Malhotra: yes role changes are logged; change events include actor, timestamp, source IP. retention we just discussed — we'll ensure it's captured in exported logs.
[02:14] Jenna Ortiz: let's talk RTO / RPO. for our patient-messaging pipeline, target RTO is 15 minutes and RPO is zero for critical messages. for other services RTO can be one hour, RPO 15 minutes. realistic?
[02:27] Alex Chen: ok that's pretty aggressive for 15 min RTO with zero RPO. can i ask — are you running this on dedicated capacity or private on-prem?
[02:35] Jenna Ortiz: private VPC deployment in our cloud account (AWS eu-central).
[02:39] Priya Malhotra: in private VPC we can offer reserved capacity with failover across AZs and optional cross-region standby. 15 min RTO for stateless endpoints is achievable; zero RPO for stateful KV cache requires synchronous replication or replication log shipping — we need to design that.
[02:54] Miguel Alvarez: what about KV cache—if cache has to be warm to meet latency? how long to warm in failover?
[03:01] Priya Malhotra: warm-up depends on prefix caching; we do progressive warming and prefetch for high-QPS routes, but full KV footprint rehydration could take tens of minutes. for zero RPO you'd want continuous replication or an active-active pattern.
[03:15] Dr. Samuel Reed: so is active-active supported? and is there a manual failover runbook?
[03:20] Alex Chen: active-active across regions is supported for certain deployments — we can design an active-passive with rapid failover too. priya will document the failover steps. we'll also provide a runbook that maps each severity to expected RTOs.
[03:32] Priya Malhotra: our runbook includes severity 1/2/3 definitions, ROEs for SRE/SE, escalation to on-call (phone + pager), and external notifications.
[03:42] Dr. Samuel Reed: wanted to understand the human escalation—who at Redwood gets paged and how fast?
[03:47] Alex Chen: for private deployments, Redwood provides an on-call rotation for platform issues; severity 1 pages within 5 minutes to the SRE on-call, then escalates to SE lead and AE if SLA-impacting. details will be in the matrix.
[03:59] Jenna Ortiz: does Redwood have an SLA credit scheme tied to availability? what counts as downtime?
[04:05] Alex Chen: yes we publish SLOs per route/model. SLA credits are pro-rated based on monthly uptime and we define downtime as inability to serve requests within contract latency thresholds — we'll share the specific SLA doc and examples.
[04:17] Miguel Alvarez: on encryption — do you support envelope encryption and customer-managed KMS keys? key rotation?
[04:24] Priya Malhotra: yes envelope encryption is standard. BYOK is supported — you bring CMKs from AWS KMS in eu-central. rotation is customer-controlled; Redwood supports key versioning and will call customer's KMS to decrypt when allowed. for HSM-backed keys we have additional controls — we'll note attestation requirements.
[04:39] Dr. Samuel Reed: how are keys stored transiently? any plaintext on nodes?
[04:43] Priya Malhotra: no persistent plaintext storage. keys are used to decrypt secrets at bootstrap and then kept in memory in an isolated process; we avoid writing keys to disk. for FIPS/HSM workflows we can minimize exposure.
[04:55] Speaker 2: quick question — regulatory evidence for audits, do you provide SOC 2 logs and change history?
[05:00] Alex Chen: yes SOC 2 Type II report, control matrices, and a collection of audit artifacts can be provided under NDA. pen test summary we can share as well.
[05:08] Dr. Samuel Reed: is the ISO scope aligned to our use case? we need ISO 27001 for vendor attestations.
[05:13] Alex Chen: Redwood is in the process of certifying under ISO 27001 (expected early 2027 in this scenario) — we can share the current ISMS scope and controls mapping today.
[05:23] Jenna Ortiz: tabletop drills—do you run joint tabletop exercises? we want to validate handoffs and paging in a simulated incident.
[05:30] Priya Malhotra: yes we do joint tabletop drills; typically a half-day session with incident simulation and postmortem artifacts. we'll run one with your SREs.
[05:38] Miguel Alvarez: ok good. for BCDR we need runbook steps for failover, DNS cutover examples, and sample playbooks for data restoration — can you provide examples?
[05:48] Priya Malhotra: yes, we have templated playbooks for DNS cutover, cache failover, and data restore from backups. we'll share sanitized examples.
[05:56] Alex Chen: i'll send the runbook and an escalations matrix. also want to call out time-to-notify: we propose 5m for severity 1, 30m for severity 2 notifications. those are configurable.
[06:08] Dr. Samuel Reed: for regulatory purposes we need a 3rd-party attestation for audit logs immutability — can Redwood support write-once immutability or send to a customer S3 with object lock?
[06:18] Priya Malhotra: yes we recommend S3 with Object Lock and cross-account replication to a Nimbus-controlled archive bucket in EU. that approach meets immutability needs.
[06:28] Jenna Ortiz: ok on metrics — we need latency breakdowns per model and per route during incidents for postmortem. do you capture token-level telemetry?
[06:36] Priya Malhotra: yes we capture token latency, queue times, kernel-switch metrics; we can stream traces to your tracing backend or provide raw csv extracts for postmortem.
[06:45] Alex Chen: closing loop on SLAs — we'll propose concrete targets for availability (99.9/99.95 options), and associated credits; we'll include examples for how credits are calculated.
[06:55] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) how quick is provisioning for a private tenant?
[07:00] Priya Malhotra: typically 2-4 weeks including infra and security reviews; for expedited engagements we can compress to 10 days with an onboarding sprint.
[07:08] Dr. Samuel Reed: last question — compliance for sub-processors and change notification? we need 30-day notice for changes that affect controls.
[07:15] Alex Chen: we provide change windows and 30-day notice for major control changes; critical security fixes follow our emergency change protocol — we'll document that.
[07:25] Jenna Ortiz: thanks — this was helpful. next steps and action items?
[07:30] Alex Chen: recap: we'll send SOC 2 Type II, iso scope docs, runbook, and KMS connector. Nimbus will provide service criticality and confirm EU-only residency. then we'll schedule the tabletop in January. any final comments?
[07:46] Dr. Samuel Reed: no, looks good. thanks alex and priya.
[07:50] Miguel Alvarez: thank you.
[07:52] Priya Malhotra: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the thread with links.

Resources / links mentioned:
- Redwood security docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/security (link to SOC/ISO artifacts)
- Runbook template (to be shared): https://redwood.ai/internal/runbooks/service-failover-template.pdf
- KMS connector spec: https://redwood.ai/docs/kms-connector (will attach)

End of transcript.
